title: Join complete thoughts with coordinating conjunctions
description: A compound sentence joins at least two independent clauses. Each clause can stand alone as a statement. And adds a related thought, but or yet shows contrast, so shows a result, or
objectives: Apply the key patterns reviewed in this activity.
Explain a correction using evidence from the sentence.
explanation: A compound sentence joins at least two independent clauses. Each clause can stand alone as a statement. And adds a related thought, but or yet shows contrast, so shows a result, or offers an alternative, for gives a reason in a more formal style, and nor continues a negative idea. Normally put a comma before a conjunction joining two full clauses. When two verbs share one subject, the structure may remain a simple sentence instead. Choose the conjunction for meaning, not merely to make a longer sentence.
examples: The room was quiet, so we could concentrate. A result joins two complete thoughts.
I wrote the draft, and my partner checked it. And adds another action with its own subject.
I wrote and checked the draft. The verbs share a subject; this is one independent clause.
correct: I was tired, so I rested.

guided.prompt: We missed the bus, ___ we walked. Choose the result linker.

independent.prompt: Complete with a contrast linker: The bag was small, ___ it was heavy.
independent.explanation: But shows a contrast between size and weight.

quiz.explanation: Both sides can stand alone.

quiz.prompt: Choose the addition linker: I made notes, ___ I reviewed them.
quiz.explanation: And adds a related thought.
